question: Determine the number of solutions of $x+2y=3$ and $kx+4y=7$ for $k=2$ and for $k\ne2$. Justify each case.
explanation:
Coefficient determinant
$$D= egin{vmatrix}1&2\k&4\end{vmatrix}=4-2k$$
Case $k e2$
When $k e2$, $D e0$. Therefore, the system has a unique solution.
Case $k=2$
The equations become $x+2y=3$ and $2x+4y=7$. The variable coefficients are proportional, but the constants are not because $2(3)=6 e7$.
Classification
Hence, the system has no solution when $k=2$ and exactly one solution when $k e2$.

options.A: For $k=2$, there are infinitely many solutions; for $k\ne2$, there is a unique solution.
options.B: For $k=2$, there is a unique solution; for $k\ne2$, there is no solution.
options.C: For $k=2$, there is no solution; for $k\ne2$, there are infinitely many solutions.
options.D: For $k=2$, there is no solution; for $k\ne2$, there is a unique solution.
